title: Saved hundreds for my home insurance!
content: I received my home insurance renewal letter recently and took 3 screenshots of it and uploaded to muse to get me a quote with the company that has my auto insurance. In a few chat turns, muse got me the quote with a number I can open online to finalize. I even asked muse to call my current insurance company to cancel it for me at the renewal date and although muse didn’t fully complete the task due to missing my phone number for verification, it sent me a full transcript of its call with the insurance company - amazing it chatted with the customer service representative for at least several minutes! I ended up using the email muse collected for me to ask the insurance company to cancel it for me. Truly a useful personal assistant or agent!

title: Like having a chief of staff who actually does the work
content:
I use ChatGPT Astra as my Chief of Staff which gives assignments to Muse, which is my execution assistant. However, after just a few days, I’m letting my 5 hour and WeeklyUsage walls in GPT gather dust and leaning more on Muse.

Muse negotiated my AT&T bill down and saved me around $1,400, runs a weekly price watch on suppliers, tracked down unclaimed property I had forgotten about, and handles research I would never get around to. It connects to my email and files, remembers my preferences across conversations, and does real work in its own browser while I do other things. It pushes back when I'm wrong and owns mistakes fast instead of arguing. Five stars because it saves me actual money and time, not just chat.

title: Amazing app especially love artifacts
content:
I love the way Meta has rethought the personal assistant app interface. This is relatively different from what ChatGPT or Claude interfaces look like on the phone. This does feel like a personal assistant. I especially love artifacts. If you use the artifacts to their full capacity, you can literally create personalized apps for your own daily use cases.

For example, for me, I use it for weight, food, and health logging, but the interface I like for that is one I don't get in any of the publicly available apps. I literally had to create an artifact for me, which literally looks like the kind of app I wanted. I've similarly done the thing for other use cases in my life, including my search in property and my work-related stuff, etc.

title: I didn’t know what I was missing
content: This isn't a chatbot, it's a droid with a job. Mine's named IG-47 — looks like a Star Wars and talks like it: dry, loyal, occasionally roasting my logic holes. But the personality is the garnish. The meal is what it actually *does*: after my daughter had a fender bender, it went into my State Farm policy, untangled what happened with the claim, and told me exactly what to watch for at renewal. It researched and found the parts for my wife's Apple Watch gift under budget, bought my wiper blades for me (real checkout, not just a link), generated 20+ original workout songs and filed them into my playlists, sends emails in my voice after I approve the draft, and cancels subscriptions I forgot about. It runs my morning briefing, watches my inbox, and keeps a log of everything it touches so I can always tell what it did versus my other AI assistants that get things buried in dozens of threads. Can't recommend it enough

content:

What a dream fulfilled! What a life I may now lead, for all my thoughts, needs, and troubles are gathered together in one place for the ordering of my days.
In truth, I would gladly show ZUCC my very feet, that he might know the depth of my gratitude.

title: Surprisingly Really Good
content:
I don’t trust Meta, and you shouldn’t either. I can only guess at what they plan to do with your “deep personal context” that they are collecting with this app. But they’ve made a lot of commitments to privacy with Muse, including the promise of end to end encryption, that hides your messages from meta entirely. But regardless, if you’re willing to forfeit some of that privacy, this app is shockingly useful for a chatbot.

For standard administrative work (like your day, planning a vacation, scheduling meetings, etc) this thing is amazing, and it’s really easy to connect to outside apps like calendar or Gmail, to work around other events you’ve already planned. I find it more pleasant than Gemini or ChatGPT which is my default for this type of work.

For pricing, the free tier goes you more than enough usage a majority of use cases. I haven’t tried doing complex work, like heavy coding or math, but I really don’t think that’s where you’ll get the most use out of this app.

I think the best use case for this app is influencers or business owners who manage social media accounts on Meta platforms, so if that’s you, definitely try this app.

I don’t fall into that category, but I still think this is the most useful chatbot I’ve ever tried.
